transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
Hello, Doctor. My husband and I were in a car accident about three weeks ago, and I can’t remember important parts of it. It really bothers me that there’s just this blank where that night should be.
Are you having any other memory problems, or is it only the events around the car accident that you can't recall?

The actual blank space is just about those specific moments of the crash itself. However, my head has felt very cloudy lately, and I keep losing track of what I'm doing during simple things like following a recipe or reading along during Bible study.
Can you recall events from before or after the accident clearly, and is there any part of your memory that feels like it's been blocked intentionally or is just hard to access?

I can remember everything before and after the crash just fine, but there is a big blank space between seeing that car slide toward us and suddenly being outside on the road with people talking to me. No matter how hard I try to replay it, those missing pieces feel completely inaccessible to me. It is like that part of the night is just gone.
Have you noticed any confusion or difficulty recognizing familiar people or places, or has your memory loss been limited to the accident and minor day-to-day lapses?

No, I have no trouble recognizing my family, friends, or familiar places; the actual memory loss is just limited to that blank space during the crash. However, my head has been very cloudy, and I often lose track of simple tasks or feel like I'm moving through a foggy dream where my surroundings don't quite feel real.
When you say things feel like a foggy dream, do you ever feel disconnected from yourself or like you're observing your own actions from outside your body?

Yes, that is exactly what it feels like. I often feel like I am moving through a foggy dream where my house and even my own hands don't really belong to me. It is like I'm watching my life unfold from a distance, wondering if this is really happening to me.
Do these feelings of being detached from yourself or the world around you only started after the accident, or have you had similar experiences at other times in your life?

No, I have never experienced anything like this before in my entire life. These strange feelings of being in a dream and detached from myself only started after the accident, about two or three weeks ago. It is very unsettling to feel so far away from my own life.

Besides the memory gap for the accident and these dream-like feelings, have you had any trouble learning new information or remembering things from your past, such as names, appointments, or personal events?

No, I haven't had any trouble remembering older memories, names, or appointments from my past. However, I do find myself losing track of what I'm doing in the moment—like following a recipe or reading during Bible study—because my head has felt so cloudy since the accident.
Do these episodes of feeling detached or in a dream happen all the time, or are they triggered by stress, reminders of the accident, or other specific situations?

They actually happen quite often and feel pretty constant throughout the day, rather than just being triggered by specific moments. Ever since the accident a few weeks ago, I've felt like I'm in this foggy dream almost all the time.
